distinctions_recorded:
THE ONE REAL CANDIDATE, and the whys separate it. cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py's discipline paragraph says instrumentation is 'targeted and TEMPORARY... not standing probes left hanging: a permanent firehose turns CC's mailbox into noise', citing the shrinking-footprint principle. A standing emitter on the inference path is permanent by construction, so on its face this collides with the floor's own charter. IT IS NOT EXCLUSIVE-AND-TERMINAL, and the reason is in that same file's history rather than in my reading of it: the paragraph was written when home was CC's in-memory MAILBOX, and its concern is a live process being flooded. The file's own 'WHAT THAT REPLACED' section records that home became a FILE on 2026-08-18 and that the plug outlived the socket. A file that a 30-day sweep forgets — child (3) of this same parent — has no firehose to be. What survives from that paragraph is the GRAIN bound, not the duration bound: 'never every function call, or every heartbeat', which is Akien's own wording in the brief that bore the parent. THE DISTINCTION TO RECORD: the discipline paragraph's 'temporary' is about a TARGETED instrument placed to catch a specific flake, and this is a STANDING trail at a named boundary. Both are legitimate and they are different acts; the file does not yet say so, and that is a charter delta the build owes.

CHECKED AND CLEAR, TWO MORE. (i) import_sieve is the sole path to the inference host — this adds no route: a module-scoped trail reaches cairn.tools.base.address and cairn.tools.base.breadcrumb_log, both leaves at the floor, and opens no socket. (ii) diagnostic.py's boot-order law ('stdlib only, no DB, no loguru, no sink backend') — already re-measured and restated in that file on 2026-08-18 for exactly these two in-house imports; this cast adds nothing beyond them.

NO COLLISION WITH SIBLING CHILDREN: (1) a-device-logs-without-being-wired is DONE and is what this composes; (3) the-logs-tree-forgets-after-30-days sweeps the root this writes into and is uncast; (4) a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads is built and is why a proof of this one cannot seed the tree it reads.

THE ASSUMPTION THAT DIED DURING THE COMPLETENESS CHECK, recorded because it makes the claim smaller and truer. I had taken it that BreadcrumbLog was reachable only through DiagnosticBase, which would have made the floor work mandatory before anything could log. It is not — BreadcrumbLog(device, instance) is a plain constructor and any module can build one and hand it a record TODAY, with no new code. So the floor seam is not load-bearing for 'can a module log at all'; it is load-bearing for 'is there exactly ONE author of the record shape', since the shape (ts/us/source/gate/pointer/values/home) is built inside DiagnosticBase.emit and a second author is a second thing to keep in step with the inspector that reads it.

THE GRAIN DECISION, made at this cast rather than left to the build: ONE record per inference call at the outcome, carrying the host that answered and the rungs walked past as a VALUE on that record — never one record per rung. /intent left these in unnoticed tension (its falsifier wanted 'which host answered', its wrong-intent clause forbade a record per rung), and host.py's resolver WALKS rungs cheapest-first on HostUnreachable, so the two collide in the ordinary case. A walk is one crossing with a path, not three crossings. This keeps an ordinary cheapest-first resolution from reading as three failures while still answering 'why was it slow'.

AT THE CLOSE (2026-08-18): THE BUILD IS DEVICE-LOCAL, NOT A FLOOR SEAM, AND THE THREE RECORDS NOW SAY SO. The cast and constrain both opened on 'cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py — a module-scoped trail', on orient's premise that a component without a device class cannot reach its trail. THE SURVEY MEASURED THAT PREMISE FALSE (its fifth absence, driven rather than reasoned at n=1: a DiagnosticBase subclass carrying cairn.devices.inference_domain.domain as its __module__, set_diagnostic_roots(tmp), one emit → home='sent' and a file on disk that did not exist before the call). So the build filled LESS than the bounds allowed: a private subclass in domain.py and three emit sites, and NOTHING under cairn/tools/. Measured at acceptance: `git diff --stat 9163ffc..HEAD -- cairn/tools/` prints nothing. A shared floor helper is still genuinely absent in the narrow sense — the one prior user hand-rolls the same five lines — but the absence is DUPLICATION AT n=2, not inability, and build-minimal does not buy an abstraction for a second user. Read the `children` field above as the cast-time premise, corrected here, not as the shape of what was built.

SPEND CAME OFF THE TRAIL, AND THE MEASUREMENT KILLED IT RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. The first build put the stored cost and the avoided counter on the hit line; the line came back DEGRADED — BreadcrumbLog replaced `values` with {} plus `values_unwritable`, because a postgres Decimal is not JSON and the trail is a JSONL file. The available fix was to coerce; the right fix was to CUT. The row already holds the spend the line points at, and one number kept in two records is a number that can drift — which is precisely what this ticket's own agreement clause (c) forbids. THE SPLIT, now a regression tooth: THE TRAIL SAYS WHAT THE CALL DID; THE METER SAYS WHAT IT COST.

THIS BUILD REPRODUCED a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads AND THEN GAVE IT A NEW MOUTH. Running the six standing device proofs BARE during the build wrote 24 records into the LIVE ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl — 14 miss / 6 hit / 4 refused, every miss naming host='fake-host', all inside 0.3 seconds — spoiling this ticket's own before-witness (censused, then moved aside through bin/cmd/trash, and the witness re-taken). The new mouth is measured and permanent: under the tester's instance seal, test_inference_domain.py now reports wrote_to_instance count 1, path 'logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl' — a proof that never touched the logs tree before this voyage now writes to it, and the ONLY thing keeping that out of the live tree is the seal. THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is now a standing fact about this device: A PROOF OF inference_domain MUST BE RUN UNDER THE TESTER, NEVER BARE. Its probe reads the live trail against the live store, so a bare run does not merely litter — it feeds the instrument false population.

THE FLOOR'S DISCIPLINE PARAGRAPH IS OWED A DELTA THIS VOYAGE DELIBERATELY DID NOT WRITE. cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py says instrumentation is 'targeted and TEMPORARY... not standing probes left hanging'; this is a STANDING trail at a named boundary, and both acts are legitimate. Writing that distinction into diagnostic.py would have put a diff hunk under cairn/tools/ and falsified this ticket's own criterion 5 instrument at the moment it was measured. Recorded in inference_domain's charter (how_it_learns) where it costs nothing, and owed as a separate act at the floor's own address rather than smuggled in here.

THE TOOL CALLS AS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE CHART (/sail step 9, a hand's act — nothing counts or observes them yet; ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart). THE COUNT FIRST, because it needs no judgement: roughly 90 tool calls between the validate berth and done, hand-counted across a compaction boundary and therefore an estimate rather than a measurement — high for a build this small, and the score reads DOWNWARD on the packet. FIVE NAMED FALSIFICATIONS, each with the leg it indicts. (1) ORIENT: its premise that a component without a device class cannot reach its trail — falsified by the survey's own driven n=1 (a DiagnosticBase subclass carrying domain as __module__, one emit, home='sent', a file on disk). (2) CONSTRAIN: its `in` list opened with a floor seam authored from that false premise, so the bounds licensed a build twice the size of the one needed. (3) VALIDATE, criterion 5: `grep -n '\"inference_domain\"' domain.py` was authored without opening domain.py, where CACHE_OWNER already matched — an instrument that cannot pass on a file it never read. (4) HYPOTHESIZE, piece 7: its non-vacuity instrument specified removing the emit and re-running BY HAND, which is a hand act on the code under test rather than a tooth; what shipped moves the world instead and runs on every future invocation. (5) VALIDATE, criterion 6: it named 'the emit chokepoint at the WATCHME crossing' as the instrument, but the emission gate renders on the crossing OFF WatchMe — at PROVED, which is AFTER the verdict that must carry the measurement. The chart authored an obligation whose instrument could not run before the artifact that reports it; the fix was to call transitions.inspect_emission directly. AND ONE FINDING ABOUT THE SURVEY STAGE ITSELF, not about this voyage: every file opened at the close — verdict.py, transitions.py, clearance.py, validation_store.py — was absent from survey's holdings, because survey inventories what the BUILD composes and says nothing about what the CLOSE needs. So the close's doors get re-derived every voyage, which is Law 1's defect wearing a routine face.
falsifier:
FALSIFIER, refined from /intent's first cut and tightened at the second clause: DONE when (a) a real inference call — not a fixture — leaves a record at ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl, read back BY OPENING THE FILE and never by asking the object whether it logged; (b) that record names the host that answered and whether the call was a hit or a miss; and (c) THE TRAIL AND THE METER AGREE — the count of miss records in the trail equals the count of verdict='miss' rows landed in the inference_calls table over the same window. Clause (c) is the one that makes this falsifiable rather than merely satisfiable: the domain already records every call in a store, so the trail is a SECOND record of the same events, and two records of one event that disagree are worse than one record (Law 7). It also means the proof cannot pass by writing its own evidence — the store is written by resolve(), not by the trail.

WRONG INTENT IF, and both directions are named because the grain can fail either way: a record per rung of the nest walk turns an ordinary cheapest-first resolution into what reads as three failures; a record only at ANSWER leaves the refusals — the case the logging exists FOR — invisible. Either would mean the seam shipped and the picture did not.

HORIZON: the next inference call the system actually makes, which needs no clock and no new instrument — the domain is the sole path, so any real traffic tests this. Bounded above by the parent's own crossing: every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree cannot cross PROVED before its children, and this is child (2).

gates:
code-seam invariant, transcribed onto this node: PROVED, and feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8).

PROVE GATE — the tester runs proofs beside each component this touches: cairn/tools/base/proofs/ for the module-scoped trail, and cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/ for the call sites. CHECK-TYPE is deterministic-and-on-disk, and the tooth a hollow build could not pass is stated as a bound rather than a suggestion: an inference call is driven through resolve() with a stub resolver against a TEMP roots table, and the record is then found BY OPENING THE FILE at log_path('inference_domain', 0, roots) and parsing the line — never by reading the return value of emit(), never by asking a mock what it received. A hollow build that shapes a record and drops it passes every object-side assertion and fails this one.

SECOND TOOTH, THE AGREEMENT CLAUSE: over one driven window, miss records in the trail are counted against verdict='miss' rows the same run landed in inference_calls, and the two must be equal. This is what the proof cannot write both sides of — the store half is written by resolve()'s existing path.

ISOLATION is set_diagnostic_roots / a temp roots table, not a hand-wired receiver: diagnostic.py's own docstring says a proof wanting isolation should reach for the roots seam because wiring a receiver 'would quietly prove the receiver instead of the default', and the default IS the mechanism under test. The instance seal (child 4) is the belt to that braces.

how:
TWO points were asserted wrapped at /intent and one of them was not.

WRAPPED AND HOLDING: the device-ness question. /intent settled it — inference_domain does not become a BaseDevice to obtain logging, because its own charter defers the runtime face on independent grounds and DiagnosticBase derives everything it needs from an address a module also has. That is a real resolution with a reason, not a deferral.

NOT WRAPPED, AND IT IS THE GRAIN. /intent's falsifier says a record must name 'which host answered and whether the answer was a hit or a miss', and its wrong-intent clause says a record per rung of the nest walk would make an ordinary cheapest-first resolution look like three failures. Those two are in tension and I did not notice at birth: host.py's resolver WALKS rungs on HostUnreachable, so 'which host answered' is only knowable by observing the walk, and observing the walk is the thing the wrong-intent clause warns against. The resolution, and it is a decision this cast makes rather than defers: ONE record per inference call at the outcome, carrying the host that answered and the rungs it had to walk past as a VALUE on that record — not one record per rung. A walk is one crossing with a path, not three crossings. This is what keeps 'starting an inference call' a single readable line and still answers 'why was it slow'.

MEASURED FIRST, and the measurement moved the approach off the one the parent assumed. `grep -c 'emit(' cairn/devices/inference_domain/` returns 0 — not 'few', none — and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: emit() lives on DiagnosticBase, DiagnosticBase is composed onto BaseDevice, and inference_domain HAS NO CLASS. domain.py, host.py and route.py are modules of functions; `resolve()`, `ollama_resolver()` and `route()` are where the crossings happen and none of them has a `self`. So the parent's phrase 'inference_domain gains an emitter' cannot be satisfied by adding emit sites — there is nothing to add them to.

THE DEVICE-NESS QUESTION, ANSWERED THE CHEAP WAY. The expensive answer is to give inference_domain a BaseDevice class. Its own charter refuses that on independent grounds — 'the BaseDevice introspection FACE and bus-fronting are the runtime face — deferred until a prober/runtime pulls them' — and building the device face in order to obtain logging would be building it for a reason that is not its reason. The cheap answer is that DiagnosticBase already derives EVERYTHING it needs from `type(self)`: the device name from `type(self).__module__` through `address.component_of_module`, the source from `type(self).__name__`, the instance from a default of 0. A module has all three facts in `__name__`. So the seam is a module-scoped trail on the floor — a small DiagnosticBase whose device and source come from a module address instead of a class address — held at module level and emitted through. It composes the default receiver, the held-not-lost semantics, the record shape and `set_diagnostic_roots` (the proof-isolation seam) without rebuilding one of them.

THE GRAIN IS ALREADY WRITTEN. The charter names the crossings: RECEIVE -> CANONICALIZE -> lookup -> (hit) VERIFY -> ANSWER, or (miss) METER -> RESOLVE -> RECORD -> ANSWER. Akien's 'starting an inference call' is the miss branch's RESOLVE — the point where it actually leaves for a host — and the hit branch is the interesting negative: a cache hit is a boundary NOT crossed, and saying so is what makes the trail readable against the meter it already keeps.
intention: Starting an inference call leaves a record on disk, so the sole path to every inference host stops being the one boundary in the system that crosses silently.
provenance: Named as child (2) when the parent was cast 2026-08-18; cast in its own right the same day after the measurement above showed the parent's phrasing could not be built as written. The device-ness question the parent handed this child is ANSWERED here and answered cheap: inference_domain does NOT become a BaseDevice to obtain logging. Its charter defers the runtime face on independent grounds ('the BaseDevice introspection FACE and bus-fronting are the runtime face — deferred until a prober/runtime pulls them'), and building that face in order to get a log would be building it for a reason that is not its reason. DiagnosticBase already derives everything it needs from an ADDRESS — the device name from type(self).__module__ through address.component_of_module, the source from the class name, the instance from a default of 0 — and a module has all three facts in __name__.
traces_to: Law 7 first — 'errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces'. The inference path is the surface where a red is least readable from anywhere else: host.py walks a nest of rungs cheapest-first and refuses when the walk exhausts, and today that whole walk happens with no record, so a mind arriving at an inference red has the traceback and nothing about the route that produced it. Law 3 second, and it is the sharper one: the domain's whole point is that the meter turns calls into evidence, and its charter says so ('the meter IS the learning surface'). A crossing that leaves no record is an observation not taken. Also Telos 1 by the parent's line — the yield report can say what inference COST and cannot say what it DID.

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying the two counts, the window, and the SPECIFIC canonical hashes present in one record and absent from the other — because 'they disagree by 4' is a finding nobody can act on and 'these four calls are in the store and not the trail' is one somebody can open.
watchme.consumer: inference_domain's owner — the same reader who reads yield_report, since the disagreement is a fact about that meter's completeness as much as about the trail
watchme.enough: cleared when enough real calls have crossed to judge (a floor, honestly placed and re-tunable once inference traffic is a measured number rather than a hoped-for one) AND every one of them appears in both records. At that moment the question is answered — the boundary is logging and the two records agree — and a standing watch on a settled question is the re-derivation Law 1 refuses.
watchme.trigger: the trail and the meter DISAGREE over the window since the seam landed — verdict='miss' rows standing in the inference_calls table with no matching record in ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl, or trail records naming calls the store never got. Fires on the disagreement, never on volume: a busy day is not a finding. Also fires on the absence that looks like nothing — misses in the store and NO trail at all, which is what a lost emitter looks like from the outside and is invisible to any check that reads the trail's contents.

why:
AKIEN, 2026-08-18, naming this example himself: 'every single everyting is supposed to log major boundry crossings and state changes. that doesn't mean every function call, or every heartbeat from the ground loop... but STARTING AN INFERENCE CALL SURE SHOULD.' MEASURED THE SAME DAY, and the measurement moved the build rather than confirming the plan: `grep -c 'emit(' cairn/devices/inference_domain/` returns ZERO — not few, none — and not from oversight. emit() lives on DiagnosticBase, DiagnosticBase is composed onto BaseDevice, and inference_domain HAS NO CLASS: domain.py, host.py and route.py are modules of functions, so resolve(), ollama_resolver() and route() have no `self` for emit() to be a method on. The parent's cast phrase 'inference_domain gains an emitter' is therefore unsatisfiable as written.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM. host.py's resolver shakes a nest of routes, dials the survivors cheapest-first, walks to the next rung on HostUnreachable, and refuses loudly when the walk exhausts. All of that happens today with no record. A mind arriving at an inference red has a traceback and nothing about the route that produced it — which host was tried, in what order, what each one said — so it re-explores by hand, and that is the exact cost diagnostic_inspector's charter exists to remove.

AND IT IS A GAP IN THE DOMAIN'S OWN CLAIM, which is the sharper half. The charter says 'the meter IS the learning surface' and the domain records every call in inference_calls — including, since 2026-08-18, the ones that RAISE. So the domain already knows what each call COST and cannot say what it DID. The trail is the second half of a record the store opened.
